title: Quad Leaders Announce First Joint Patrol-Aircraft Exercise and Critical Minerals Deals in Manila
excerpt: The Manila summit’s joint statement pairs a 2027 P-8 exercise and a business forum with a warning on economic coercion — while leaving the South China Sea unnamed.
body:
• The first Quad leaders’ summit in two years ended in Manila with a joint statement announcing the first-ever Quad maritime exercise involving patrol aircraft — the four countries’ P-8 and P-3C planes will fly together in 2027 under a new Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration.
  • The leaders expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export curbs, and committed to securing critical supply chains; President Trump said the four had reached new critical minerals deals, though no values or texts were released.
  • An inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum will be held in early 2027, and the leaders launched an Enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation and backed wider deployment of trusted AI.
  • The statement strongly opposed unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion — but, unlike the 2024 Wilmington Declaration, it did not explicitly name the South or East China Seas.

The Quad’s first leaders’ summit in two years produced a short joint statement and a cluster of firsts. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met in Manila on Tuesday evening, November 17, for about 90 minutes on the sidelines of the ASEAN-related summits, and issued a joint press release committing the four countries to a first joint patrol-aircraft exercise, new supply-chain work and a business forum — while pointedly warning against economic coercion without naming China.

What was announced

The centrepiece is maritime. Under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, an initiative to share information and build maritime domain awareness across the region, patrol aircraft of the four countries — P-8 and P-3C planes — will fly in a maritime exercise in 2027 for the first time in a Quad context, according to the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office summary of the summit. Trump announced the exercise for March 2027 in Guam, The Times of India reported. The leaders also committed to ensuring open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific and to protecting freedom of navigation and overflight.

On supply chains, the four confirmed they will work together on critical minerals resilience and energy security. Trump said the Quad nations had reached several new critical mineral deals so that none of them remained vulnerable to coercion by a single foreign supplier; no deal values, counterparties or texts were released with the statement. The leaders announced that the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum will be held in early 2027, launched an “Enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation” in response to rising cyber incidents, and backed the AI Accelerator — an effort to coordinate and fund trusted AI access across the Indo-Pacific, first announced by the four foreign ministers on the margins of the G20 meeting in Atlanta.

“From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific.”

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, at the Manila summit

The signal to Beijing — and its limits

The statement’s language on China was firm in principle and careful in naming. The leaders expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export curbs, and strongly opposed “any destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion.” They condemned terrorism and violent extremism, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening counterterrorism cooperation. But the short release did not explicitly mention the South China Sea or the East China Sea — a contrast with the expansive 2024 Wilmington Declaration that, as The Times of India noted, cut Beijing some slack. The timing underlined the calibration: the Manila meeting took place hours before Trump’s departure for China, where he was set to attend a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

What Modi said, and what comes next

Modi called the meeting an important milestone and described the Quad as a trusted partnership for India. Trump, in his opening remarks, called the grouping very important and said it would work to protect “peace through strength.” The statement recalled that this year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the free and open Indo-Pacific vision first articulated by the late Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2016. With India unable to host the summit for the past two years, Modi pitched a leaders’ meeting in early 2027, The Times of India reported; the joint release did not acknowledge a next summit. The first dated tests of Tuesday’s statement are the business forum in early 2027 and the patrol-aircraft exercise later that year.
